title: Teachers appointed
summary: King Laman appoints Amulon and his brethren as teachers among his people, while kings govern the lands the Lamanites possess.

explicit_facts.text: Amulon gained favor with the king of the Lamanites, who appointed him and his brethren as teachers over his people, including in Shemlon, Shilom, and Amulon.
The Lamanites had taken possession of these lands, and the king appointed kings over them.
The king was named Laman after his father and ruled a numerous people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king and Amulon with his brethren are together for the appointment.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the king, Amulon, and his brethren; the site and ceremony of appointment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unreported coronation, meeting venue, or distinct subordinate kings.

title: The language taught
summary: Teachers from among Amulon's brethren teach the language of Nephi, record-keeping, and writing to one another, but not the Lord, the law of Moses, or Abinadi's words.

explicit_facts.text: Teachers appointed from among Amulon's brethren taught the language of Nephi among the Lamanites.
The people were friendly with one another but did not know God, and the brethren of Amulon did not teach them about the Lord, the law of Moses, or Abinadi's words.
The teachers taught them to keep records and write to one another.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Teachers instructing Lamanites in writing is a visual way to represent the reported teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the instruction happens in a classroom or outdoors; writing materials and clothing.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific lesson about God or the law of Moses; the verses say these were not taught.

title: Trade and plunder
summary: The Lamanites increase in riches and trade with one another; the account describes their worldly cunning and plunder beyond their own people.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites increased in riches, traded with one another, and became cunning and wise in worldly matters; they delighted in wickedness and plunder except among their own brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Trading can be represented by Lamanites exchanging goods.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific goods, market setting, and any particular act of plunder.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The description of cunning and worldly wisdom is narration, not a separate visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific raid or victim not identified in the text.

title: Alma's people put under authority
summary: Amulon exercises authority over Alma and his brethren, persecutes them, and imposes tasks and taskmasters; their children are also made to persecute Alma's people's children.

explicit_facts.text: Amulon began exercising authority over Alma and his brethren, persecuting him and causing his children to persecute their children.

Amulon knew Alma had been one of the king's priests, believed Abinadi's words, and had been driven out before the king; Amulon was wroth with him, was subject to King Laman, and imposed tasks and taskmasters on Alma's people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Taskmasters imposing work on Alma's people conveys the reported authority and tasks.
unspecified_visual_details: The particular tasks, appearance of the taskmasters, and location of the work.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's past as a priest and his expulsion are reported background, not a depicted past scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier expulsion before the king as happening now.

title: Silent prayer under guard
summary: Alma's people suffer and pray in their hearts. Amulon orders them not to cry aloud and places guards over them, threatening death for anyone found calling upon God.

explicit_facts.text: Their afflictions led them to cry mightily to God.
Amulon ordered them to stop their cries, set guards to watch them, and ordered that anyone found calling upon God be put to death.
Alma and his people did not raise their voices to the Lord but poured out their hearts to him, and he knew their thoughts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's people praying silently while guards watch represents the contrast described.
unspecified_visual_details: The form of their silent prayer and the guards' arrangement.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord knowing their thoughts is stated in narration; no visible appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lord visibly; do not depict an execution.

title: The voice of the Lord promises deliverance
summary: The voice of the Lord comes to people in their afflictions, promising comfort, a covenant, deliverance from bondage, and relief from their burdens.
characters: The Lord, heard as a voice

explicit_facts.text: The voice of the Lord came to the people in their afflictions.
The Lord said he knew of their covenant with him and promised to covenant with his people and deliver them from bondage.
The Lord promised to ease the burdens on their shoulders while they were still in bondage, so they could later be witnesses and know that he visits his people in their afflictions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown listening, with burdens on their shoulders.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the people's appearance.
Any visible source of the voice.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lift up your heads and be of good comfort, for I know of the covenant which ye have made unto me;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and I will covenant with my people and deliver them out of bondage.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: And I will also ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: even while you are in bondage;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is heard as a voice; no visible appearance is described.
The easing of burdens is a promise in this passage, not a separately narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a visible divine figure or a visible source for the voice.
Do not depict deliverance or the easing of burdens as already occurring.
Do not identify the people or location beyond what these verses state.

title: Burdens made light
summary: The burdens on Alma and his brethren are made light; the Lord strengthens them, and they bear their burdens with ease and submit cheerfully and patiently.

explicit_facts.text: The burdens laid upon Alma and his brethren were made light, and the Lord strengthened them to bear their burdens with ease; they submitted cheerfully and patiently to the Lord's will.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's people continuing their work with patient expressions can represent the reported endurance.
unspecified_visual_details: The tasks being performed and any visible sign of the burdens becoming lighter.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The easing and strengthening are stated as events; no physical manifestation is specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural glow or other unstated visual effect.

title: Promise of deliverance
summary: The Lord speaks again, promising deliverance on the morrow and telling Alma that he will lead the people, with the Lord going with him.

explicit_facts.text: Because of their faith and patience, the voice of the Lord came again, promising deliverance from bondage on the morrow.
The Lord told Alma to go before the people and promised to go with him and deliver them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown receiving the voice's message.
unspecified_visual_details: How the Lord's voice is represented; Alma's precise posture or surroundings.

spoken_dialogue.text: Be of good comfort, for on the morrow I will deliver you out of bondage.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Thou shalt go before this people,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and I will go with thee and deliver this people out of bondage.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is heard as a voice; no visible appearance is given.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly.

title: Gathering in the night
summary: During the night, Alma and his people gather their flocks and grain.

explicit_facts.text: At night Alma and his people gathered their flocks and grain, continuing throughout the night.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People gathering livestock and grain by night.
unspecified_visual_details: The quantity and type of livestock and grain; lighting and tools.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show departure yet; it occurs in the following verses.

title: The Lamanites sleep
summary: In the morning, a deep sleep comes upon the Lamanites, including all their taskmasters.

explicit_facts.text: In the morning the Lord caused a deep sleep to come upon the Lamanites, and all their taskmasters were in a profound sleep.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites and taskmasters are shown asleep in the morning.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact place where they sleep and their positions.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's action is explicitly attributed in the account, but no visible divine manifestation is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a visible figure causing the sleep.

title: Into the wilderness
summary: Alma and his people depart into the wilderness, travel all day, and pitch their tents in a valley they name Alma.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and his people departed into the wilderness and, after traveling all day, pitched their tents in a valley called Alma because Alma led their way.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The journey can be shown as movement from the place of bondage into the wilderness, ending with tents in the valley.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, landscape, and number or appearance of tents.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a specific route or landmark.

title: Thanks in the valley
summary: In the valley of Alma, the people give thanks to God for mercy, eased burdens, and deliverance; men, women, and speaking children praise God aloud.

explicit_facts.text: In the valley of Alma, they gave thanks to God for his mercy, the easing of their burdens, and deliverance from bondage; they said none could deliver them except the Lord their God.
All the men and women and children able to speak lifted their voices in praise of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown gathered in the valley praising God.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether they stand, kneel, or gather in a particular formation.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Their thanks and praise are narrated; no exact words of prayer are supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a quotation for their prayer.

title: Leave the valley
summary: The Lord warns Alma that the Lamanites have awakened and are pursuing, commands the people to leave, and promises to stop the pursuers in the valley. Alma's people depart into the wilderness.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord told Alma to hurry out of the land because the Lamanites had awakened and were pursuing them, and promised to stop the Lamanites in the valley.
Alma's people departed from the valley and journeyed into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people can be shown departing the valley into the wilderness after hearing the warning.
unspecified_visual_details: The form in which the Lord's warning is received; the pursuers' distance and appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Haste thee and get thou and this people out of this land,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: for the Lamanites have awakened and do pursue thee;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: therefore get thee out of this land,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and I will stop the Lamanites in this valley that they come no further in pursuit of this people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is described as speaking; no visible appearance is stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lamanites being stopped; only the promise is given here.

title: Arrival in Zarahemla
summary: After twelve days in the wilderness, Alma's people arrive in Zarahemla, where King Mosiah receives them with joy.

explicit_facts.text: After twelve days in the wilderness, Alma's people arrived in the land of Zarahemla, and King Mosiah received them with joy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Mosiah and Alma's people meet upon their arrival.
unspecified_visual_details: The location of the reception within Zarahemla and the form of the welcome.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue or a specific ceremonial welcome.
